ops.title: cc-pool host-sync: origin-owned chains, stripped envelopes, and why holder/lease/lineage died
ops.body:
Supersedes `10bf17db` (stamp discipline, chain lineage, and the P2 adversarial-review
record). The holder/lease/lineage design recorded there is deleted; this note is the
current design plus the reason the old one was unfixable.

## The design: origin-owned chains, stripped envelopes

Each credential chain has exactly one **origin** — the host whose `ccp login`/`ccp add`
minted it. Origin is a static fact (which host holds the refresh token), not a leased
role. Only the origin refreshes.

**The refresh token never crosses the mesh.** The fetch RPC serves `cred.Strip()` — a
copy with the refresh token removed — so the secret never leaves the origin process.
The method is renamed `ccp.fetch_stripped_credential`: a mixed-version peer that only
knows the old name gets unknown-method, so a full-credential blob can never cross a
version-mismatched pair. Peers hold `accessToken + expiresAt` only; the origin's normal
idle refresh rotates the chain and each new access token propagates via registry stamp
+ pull, keeping peers usable indefinitely while the origin is alive.

**Ownership = refresh-token presence.** A blob with a refresh token is owned;
access-token-only is synced. Sync never replaces an owned blob; a synced blob advances
only on strictly-later expiry. A host never publishes a chain stamp for an account it
doesn't own (synced-only publishes an identity-only chain), so an empty chain can't
clobber a live origin's in the LWW merge.

**Freshness = strictly-later expiry + owned precedence.** Lineage/ParentHash deleted.
The stamp is `ChainStamp{Origin, ExpiresAt, Hash, RotatedAt}`; `Hash` is `AccessHash`,
a length-prefixed SHA-256 over the access token only — a one-way digest, never a
secret, never in SQLite. The origin is authoritative for its own chain (a
self-consistent answer ahead of the registry stamp is mirror lag, not corruption); a
relay answer must match the registry `Hash` AND `ExpiresAt` exactly, so a tampered
stamp is uninstallable.

**Peer expiry** surfaces "needs login (or wait for the origin)" — `AuthKind` =
`AwaitingOrigin` vs `Owned` — and scores as needs-login, so a dead copy sinks in
ranking. `ccp login` there mints that machine its own chain; dual-origin is allowed,
and the ORIGIN column may then alternate as each host rotates (accepted cosmetic wart).

**Self-heal:** on `invalid_grant` the daemon strips the spent refresh token from its
own blob (the double-spend loser becomes synced-shape) and pulls the winner's stripped
chain, so a chain owned by two hosts heals into origin + peer on the first double-spend.

**Teardown fails closed** (unchanged): removal only when provably idle, a uuid shared
by several rows is refused, and the registry is re-checked after claiming. `ccp doctor`
reports wedges, sync-socket health, mesh reachability, and registry corruption.

## Why holder/lease/lineage died

Claude refresh tokens are single-use: two hosts refreshing one chain double-spend it →
`invalid_grant` → Claude tombstones the credential → "Not logged in". The old design
replicated the full chain to every host and serialized refresh with a leased holder
role, plus ParentHash lineage for clock-skew-proof freshness. That serializes only the
daemons. **claude's own in-session refresh spends whatever refresh token sits in the
blob** the moment the access token expires — no daemon-side gate can win a race against
a process it doesn't control. Any design where a peer holds a spendable refresh token
has this hole; holder/lease/takeover and lineage-first freshness treated the symptom
(who refreshes, which chain is fresher) instead of the cause (peers holding the secret
at all). Removing the secret from peers is the only race-free enforcement — structural,
not a gate. It also deletes the problem lineage existed to solve: peers never mint
competing chains, so strictly-later expiry from a single origin clock suffices.

## Security fixes folded into the redesign

- **RCE via `ChainStamp.Origin`**: the registry-controlled Origin string flowed into
  the peer-transport dial target, whose `exec:` prefix reached `sh -c` — a poisoned
  registry entry was remote code execution on every puller. Fixed by intersecting dial
  targets with the trusted configured mesh and gating `exec:` behind a sim-only env var.
- **Cross-account install**: reconcile now rejects a registry entry whose key ≠
  `value.UUID`, so a crafted entry can't install one account's credential under
  another's slot.

## Residuals (open)

1. **Origin-side claude↔daemon double-spend** — claude's per-account
   `.oauth_refresh.lock` and cc-pool's `acct-NN.lock` are separate locks, so on the
   origin an in-session claude and the daemon can still both spend one single-use RT.
   The redesign shrinks the exposure (peers eliminated; the full-credential CAS refuses
   to clobber claude's winning rotation) but the origin residual needs a shared lock.
   ccn task `4ed1146`.
2. **`FinalizeAdd` id-reservation window** — ccn `5fa8ffe9`.
ops.when: Touching cc-pool host-sync — credential propagation, refresh discipline, the ChainStamp/registry format, the fetch RPC — or considering ANY cross-host refresh coordination (holders, leases, lineage, freshness gates)
